title: Dormancy Settings for Personal Checking Accounts
content:
A Personal Checking account is classified dormant after the number of calendar months without customer-initiated activity that its tier sets. While the account is dormant the tier's dormant account charge applies at each statement cycle close, and that charge never takes the ledger balance below zero.

| Tier | Calendar months without customer-initiated activity before dormancy | Dormant account charge per statement cycle (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 12 | 0.00 |
| Student Checking | 12 | 0.00 |
| Everyday Checking | 12 | 5.00 |
| Interest Checking | 12 | 5.00 |
| Premier Checking | 12 | 5.00 |
| Private Client Checking | 24 | 0.00 |

A charge of 0.00 means the tier takes nothing while the account is dormant.

**Illustration (hypothetical).** Private Client Checking is the one tier whose inactivity period is 24 calendar months rather than 12, and it also carries a dormant account charge of 0.00. An account of that tier that has seen no customer-initiated activity for 18 calendar months is therefore not yet dormant, while an account of any other tier at the same point has been dormant for 6 months.
